1	"""Task assignment, dynamic map edits and collision-aware tick execution.
2	
3	Obstacles may be closed and reopened between ticks through
4	:meth:`FleetSimulator.modify_obstacles`. Every accepted edit is appended to a
5	deterministic change history and mirrored into the replay as a ``map_change``
6	event stamped with the tick at which it took effect. Tick frames themselves are
7	never rewritten, so historical frames keep the positions and completion
8	information recorded at the time.
9	
10	Automatic yielding
11	------------------
12	When a robot's next waypoint is occupied by another robot, ``step()`` tries to
13	keep traffic flowing instead of waiting forever: a parked blocker (one with no
14	bound task *and* no remaining route) is asked to move onto a free side cell
15	that lies on no robot's planned route, and a busy robot facing a blocker that
16	cannot drive on may itself sidestep onto a free adjacent cell and replan its
17	(still shortest) route from there. A taskless robot that still carries a
18	remaining route is not parked: it drives that route cell by cell exactly like
19	a task-bound robot, is never pushed onto a side cell for someone else, and if
20	its own next cell is blocked it simply keeps its place and its unconsumed
21	waypoints -- an open side cell changes nothing. Only once such a route is
22	exhausted does the robot become a parked robot and yield by the side-cell
23	rule. Task assignment follows the same line: only a robot with no bound task
24	*and* no remaining route can receive a waiting task, so a taskless robot
25	still driving its preset route never has that route overwritten by a new
26	assignment -- being blocked by traffic along the way does not count as having
27	finished the route, and once the route runs out the robot joins the selection
28	at the next assignment pass, planned from wherever it stands then. A retreat that
29	only leads back to the same immovable blocker is never taken though: if the
30	replanned route immediately returns through the vacated cell, still passes the
31	blocker's cell and the blocker cannot use the opening to leave (a dead end or
32	corridor end with traffic parked beyond it), the robot simply waits -- extra
33	empty cells stretching out behind it change nothing. Yield moves count as
34	mileage, waiting does not. The task keeps its original robot, pickup and
35	completion rules are unchanged, and a robot paused by map unreachability never
36	takes part in yielding. If no safe side cell exists the robots simply wait:
37	time advances, nothing collides and nothing completes early. Waiting caused
38	purely by other robots is tracked per robot (consecutive ticks and the
39	blocking robot) and reported by :meth:`FleetSimulator.status` and
40	:meth:`FleetSimulator.metrics` as ``traffic_waits``, distinct from the
41	map-unreachability ``paused_tasks``. The record is judged against the
42	end-of-tick layout, not the moment the robot gave way: when a robot that was
43	asked to wait sees its next cell free at tick end (the blocker drove on or
44	made room later in the same tick), no wait is reported for that tick at all,
45	and ``blocked_by`` names whichever robot actually occupies the cell once the
46	tick settles. The counter clears the moment the robot moves again or the
47	blockage ends; an uninterrupted wait whose blocking robot merely changes
48	identity keeps accumulating with the new blocker, whereas a wait that was
49	interrupted and later recurs starts again at one. An accepted map edit
50	reconciles the records immediately: a robot paused by the new map or no
51	longer facing its recorded blocker on the replanned route loses its entry, an
52	entry still facing the same blocker keeps its count, and no edit ever creates
53	or increments one.
54	
55	Initial task ownership
56	----------------------
57	A fleet can be created mid-work: a robot may already name its current task
58	with a remaining route, and a task may already be assigned or even loaded.
59	Construction validates these bindings up front instead of discovering them
60	while stepping. Every robot that names a task must name one that exists, is
61	still unfinished and is assigned back to that robot; every unfinished task
62	that names an owner must name an existing robot whose current task it is, and
63	a task with the goods collected may never lack that owner. One robot is
64	therefore never claimed by two unfinished tasks, and a robot may never be
65	bound to a completed task. Finished tasks only retain *historical* ownership:
66	their recorded robot need not be idle or name them back, may already work a
67	new task, and may even be absent from the fleet. Unassigned, not-yet-collected
68	tasks simply wait -- including ones no robot can currently reach -- and are
69	not an ownership error. Conflicts raise :class:`ValueError` naming the robot
70	or task involved; nothing is rebound, unassigned or dropped, and the caller's
71	objects are left untouched. The same unfinished-task binding rules govern
72	checkpoint loading (which additionally keeps its historical-state checks).
73	
74	Every robot's remaining route is also validated as a walk on the given map,
75	whether or not the robot is bound to a task, and direct construction and
76	checkpoint recovery run the *same* :func:`_validate_route_walk` check, so the
77	walking rule is maintained in exactly one place. The route omits the robot's
78	current cell, so a non-empty route must begin with an up/down/left/right
79	neighbour of that cell and every later waypoint must be one orthogonal step
80	from the previous one; each waypoint must be in bounds and free of obstacles.
81	Diagonal steps, multi-cell jumps, two identical consecutive waypoints and a
82	first waypoint equal to the current position are all rejected, and waypoints
83	must be two plain integers (never booleans) in a list or tuple, with wrong
84	lengths or element types raising :class:`ValueError` rather than leaking
85	unpacking or hashing errors. Empty routes stay legal; a route need not be
86	shortest and may revisit cells. A route crossing another robot's current cell,
87	or several robots planning through the same cell, is not an error -- those
88	traffic conflicts are settled during execution. The direct interface keeps
89	its existing acceptance of a bound route's pickup/dropoff ordering and end
90	point; checkpoint loading additionally keeps its own stricter route checks
91	(including the task completion rules), its format and the map-paused
92	behaviour, under which a paused robot resumes with an empty route.
93	
94	Checkpoint file format
95	----------------------
96	``save_checkpoint`` writes versioned, UTF-8 encoded JSON. The current format
97	version is ``2``; version ``1`` files remain readable.
98	
99	``version``
100	    Integer format version (``1`` or ``2``).
101	``grid``
102	    ``{"width": int, "height": int, "obstacles": [[x, y], ...]}`` describing
103	    the map dimensions and every currently blocked cell.
104	``tick``
105	    Non-negative integer: the number of ticks already executed. Saving and
106	    loading never advance this value.
107	``robots``
108	    List of robot states, each
109	    ``{"robot_id": str, "position": [x, y], "route": [[x, y], ...],
110	    "task_id": str | null, "distance_travelled": int}``. ``route`` holds the
111	    remaining waypoints after ``position``.
112	``tasks``
113	    List of task states, each
114	    ``{"task_id": str, "pickup": [x, y], "dropoff": [x, y],
115	    "assigned_robot": str | null, "picked_up": bool, "completed": bool}``.
116	    Completed tasks keep their historical ``assigned_robot``.
117	``replay``
118	    Ordered event list. Tick events are numbered consecutively from ``1``
119	    through ``tick`` and have the shape
120	    ``{"type": "tick", "tick": int, "moved": [robot_id, ...],
121	    "robots": {robot_id: [x, y], ...}, "completed": [task_id, ...]}``.
122	    ``completed`` is the cumulative set of tasks finished by the end of that
123	    tick: entries must name checkpoint tasks without repeats within one frame,
124	    a recorded completion must survive every later frame, and the final
125	    frame's set must equal the tasks saved with ``completed: true``.
126	    Map-change events sit between ticks (or after the last tick) and look like
127	    ``{"type": "map_change", "tick": int, "sequence": int,
128	    "added": [[x, y], ...], "removed": [[x, y], ...]}``. When ``tick`` is
129	    non-zero the final tick event's robot positions must match the current
130	    robot positions.
131	``map_changes`` (version 2 only)
132	    List mirroring the replay map-change events in the same order:
133	    ``{"tick": int, "sequence": int, "added": [...], "removed": [...]}``.
134	``base_grid`` (version 2 only)
135	    ``{"width", "height", "obstacles"}`` describing the map before any runtime
136	    edit. Replaying ``map_changes`` against it must reproduce the saved current
137	    ``grid``.
138	``traffic_waits`` (optional)
139	    List of ``{"robot_id": str, "blocked_by": [str, ...], "ticks": int}``
140	    entries recording how many consecutive ticks each robot has been held up
141	    purely by other robots. Absent in older files, which load with every
142	    wait counter at zero. Each entry must agree with the saved layout: the
143	    robot needs a remaining route and ``blocked_by`` must name exactly the
144	    robot occupying its next route cell -- a next cell nobody occupies, a
145	    listed blocker parked elsewhere, or extra names beside the real blocker
146	    all reject the document.
147	
148	Version 1 documents store tick frames without a ``type`` field and have no
149	``map_changes`` or ``base_grid`` key; they load with their grid taken as the
150	baseline, as if no map edit ever happened.
151	
152	Both map definitions are validated by the single shared
153	:meth:`FleetSimulator._load_map_definition` rule -- positive integer
154	dimensions, an obstacle list of integer ``[x, y]`` pairs inside the map --
155	with wording that names the map at fault, so a format or value rule is
156	maintained in exactly one place while each map keeps its own contents. The
157	cross-definition constraints (matching dimensions and a history that replays
158	``base_grid`` onto ``grid``) are checked separately and remain distinct
159	rejection reasons from a malformed definition.
160	
161	Loading performs strict validation: malformed JSON, missing or wrongly typed
162	fields, unsupported versions, duplicate or inconsistent entities, out of
163	bounds/obstructed positions and routes, non-adjacent route steps, ownership
164	mismatches, routes that cannot finish the robot's bound task, traffic waits
165	that contradict the saved robot positions and remaining routes, broken replay
166	or map-change history, a completion history that contradicts the saved task
167	states, and a history that does not reproduce the saved grid all raise
168	:class:`ValueError`.
169	
170	A task-bound route is judged against the task's pickup state, not just for
171	walkability. For every assigned, unfinished task that is not paused by map
172	unreachability, a non-empty remaining route must end at the dropoff, and when
173	the goods are not yet collected and the robot is not already standing on the
174	pickup cell, the route must still pass through that pickup cell -- passing the
175	dropoff early changes nothing as long as the route later collects and returns,
176	and avoidance detours need not match a replanned shortest route. An empty
177	route is accepted only when a loaded robot already stands at the dropoff, or
178	when position, pickup and dropoff all coincide; paused tasks keep their
179	empty-route exemption, and unassigned or completed tasks are not checked.
180	
181	The recorded movement history is checked for physical plausibility, not just
182	for a matching final frame. In every tick frame each robot must stand on a
183	cell that is in bounds and traversable on the map of that moment, no two
184	robots may end a tick on the same cell, and from the second frame on a robot
185	may only have waited or stepped one orthogonal cell (two robots cannot swap
186	cells within one tick; following a robot into the cell it just vacated is
187	fine). A frame's ``moved`` list must reference current fleet robots without
188	duplicates and, whenever a previous frame exists, must name exactly the
189	robots whose positions changed, in any order. Version 2 map changes are
190	applied in their recorded order after the tick they are stamped on, so a
191	robot may be recorded in a cell that is closed later, may not appear in a
192	cell before it opens, and no change may add an obstacle onto a cell a tick
193	frame shows occupied -- not even when a later change of the same tick removes
194	it. Filesystem and permission failures propagate as :class:`OSError`.

214	def _is_int(value: object) -> bool:
215	    """JSON booleans are ints in Python; checkpoints treat them as wrong."""
216	    return isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool)

219	def _coordinate_pair(value: object, description: str, *, strict_list: bool) -> Position:
220	    """Validate *value* as a pair of two plain integers.
221	
222	    Booleans are rejected even though they are Python ints, and wrong lengths
223	    or element types raise :class:`ValueError` instead of leaking unpacking or
224	    hashing errors. This is the one coordinate-shape rule shared by every
225	    caller; the two entry points only differ in the outer container spellings
226	    they accept:
227	
228	    * strict JSON lists only (*strict_list* true, checkpoints, whose document
229	      shape is fixed and must not be relaxed because validation is shared);
230	    * lists or tuples alike (*strict_list* false, the direct Python interface,
231	      where the two spellings may be mixed freely).
232	    """
233	    if strict_list:
234	        # Checkpoints keep their single, fixed message for every shape problem
235	        # -- wrong type, wrong length or a non-integer (including a boolean) --
236	        # because the JSON document shape is fixed and shared validation must
237	        # not change what a malformed checkpoint reports.
238	        if (
239	            not isinstance(value, list)
240	            or len(value) != 2
241	            or not all(_is_int(coord) for coord in value)
242	        ):
243	            raise ValueError(f"{description} must be a [x, y] integer pair")
244	    else:
245	        if isinstance(value, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(value, (tuple, list)):
246	            raise ValueError(f"{description} must be a [x, y] integer pair")
247	        if len(value) != 2:
248	            raise ValueError(f"{description} must be a [x, y] integer pair")
249	        if not all(_is_int(coord) for coord in value):
250	            raise ValueError(
251	                f"{description} coordinates must be integers, not booleans or other types"
252	            )
253	    return value[0], value[1]

266	def _task_route_waypoints(origin: Position, task: Task) -> list[Position]:
267	    """Required remaining visit points after *origin* for *task*.
268	
269	    The same pickup/delivery rule is used by first-time assignment, rerouting
270	    after map changes (and the recovery/sidestep planning that shares it) and
271	    checkpoint validation, so the requirement lives in exactly one place:
272	
273	    * Goods not yet collected: the route must still reach the pickup and then
274	      the dropoff. Standing exactly on the pickup makes the pickup leg empty --
275	      the leg contributes no waypoint -- but planning never collects or
276	      completes anything by itself.
277	    * Goods already collected: the robot routes straight to the dropoff, even
278	      when the old pickup cell was closed afterwards; it is never sent back.
279	
280	    When *origin*, pickup and dropoff coincide the list is empty, which
281	    describes a feasible zero-step route and must not be confused with an
282	    unreachable one.
283	    """
284	    waypoints: list[Position] = []
285	    if not task.picked_up and origin != task.pickup:
286	        waypoints.append(task.pickup)
287	    last = waypoints[-1] if waypoints else origin
288	    if task.dropoff != last:
289	        waypoints.append(task.dropoff)
290	    return waypoints

293	def _plan_task_route(
294	    grid: GridMap, origin: Position, task: Task
295	) -> list[Position] | None:
296	    """Shortest feasible route through the task's required waypoints.
297	
298	    The returned list holds the cells after *origin* only, concatenating the
299	    deterministic shortest legs between consecutive required points. It is
300	    ``None`` when any required point cannot be reached, and an empty list for a
301	    feasible route with zero steps (origin already at the only destination).
302	    """
303	    route: list[Position] = []
304	    current = origin
305	    for waypoint in _task_route_waypoints(origin, task):
306	        try:
307	            leg = shortest_path(grid, current, waypoint)
308	        except ValueError:
309	            return None
310	        route.extend(leg)
311	        current = waypoint
312	    return route

315	def _validate_route_walk(
316	    grid: GridMap,
317	    origin: Position,
318	    route: Sequence[object],
319	    *,
320	    robot_id: str,
321	    checkpoint: bool,
322	) -> list[Position]:

324	
325	    This is the single place that owns the walking rule shared by direct
326	    fleet construction and checkpoint recovery, so the same legality check is
327	    never edited twice. A route holds the cells still ahead of *origin*:
328	
329	    * every waypoint must parse as two plain integers (booleans are rejected),
330	      lie inside the map and outside its obstacles;
331	    * the first waypoint must be an up/down/left/right neighbour of *origin*,
332	      so a first waypoint equal to the current cell is rejected;
333	    * every later waypoint must be exactly one orthogonal step from the
334	      previous one -- diagonal moves, multi-cell jumps and two identical
335	      consecutive waypoints are all rejected.
336	
337	    Detours and revisits (including *origin*) are legal, and a route crossing
338	    another robot's cell is never a walk error: traffic is settled while
339	    stepping, not here. The walkability rule deliberately says nothing about
340	    the bound task's pickup/dropoff requirements; checkpoint loading keeps
341	    that separate, stricter business check. The result is a fresh mutable list
342	    of tuple cells, so validating never aliases or mutates the caller's
343	    container and a rejected input leaves every earlier object untouched.
344	
345	    The two entries keep their existing format and wording differences via
346	    *checkpoint*: direct construction (false) accepts a list or tuple route of
347	    list-or-tuple cells and reports ``route waypoint N`` with a dedicated
348	    message for a first waypoint on the current cell and for repeated
349	    consecutive waypoints; checkpoint loading (true) keeps the strict JSON
350	    list-of-lists format (``_as_pair``), says ``route entry`` and folds both
351	    equal-cell cases into its existing non-adjacency message. The checks
352	    performed are identical either way.
353	    """
354	    waypoints: list[Position] = []
355	    previous = origin
356	    for index, cell in enumerate(route):
357	        if checkpoint:
358	            waypoint = _as_pair(
359	                cell, f"robot {robot_id!r} route entry {index}"
360	            )
361	        else:
362	            waypoint = _as_cell(
363	                cell, f"robot {robot_id!r} route waypoint {index}"
364	            )
365	        if not grid.traversable(waypoint):
366	            if checkpoint:
367	                raise ValueError(
368	                    f"robot {robot_id!r} route entry {list(waypoint)} is "
369	                    "outside the map or inside an obstacle"
370	                )
371	            raise ValueError(
372	                f"robot {robot_id!r} route waypoint {index} "
373	                f"{list(waypoint)} is outside the map or inside an obstacle"
374	            )
375	        if waypoint == previous:
376	            if checkpoint:
377	                # The checkpoint wording treats an equal cell like any other
378	                # non-adjacent step, naming both cells of the offending move.
379	                raise ValueError(
380	                    f"robot {robot_id!r} route moves non-adjacently from "
381	                    f"{list(previous)} to {list(waypoint)}"
382	                )
383	            if index == 0:
384	                raise ValueError(
385	                    f"robot {robot_id!r} route waypoint 0 {list(waypoint)} "
386	                    "is the robot's current cell; the remaining route must "
387	                    "start with the next cell"
388	                )
389	            raise ValueError(
390	                f"robot {robot_id!r} route repeats cell {list(waypoint)} at "
391	                f"consecutive waypoints {index - 1} and {index}"
392	            )
393	        if (
394	            abs(waypoint[0] - previous[0])
395	            + abs(waypoint[1] - previous[1])
396	            != 1
397	        ):
398	            if checkpoint:
399	                raise ValueError(
400	                    f"robot {robot_id!r} route moves non-adjacently from "
401	                    f"{list(previous)} to {list(waypoint)}"
402	                )
403	            if index == 0:
404	                segment = (
405	                    f"from its current position {list(previous)} to route "
406	                    f"waypoint 0 {list(waypoint)}"
407	                )
408	            else:
409	                segment = (
410	                    f"from route waypoint {index - 1} {list(previous)} to "
411	                    f"waypoint {index} {list(waypoint)}"
412	                )
413	            raise ValueError(
414	                f"robot {robot_id!r} route moves non-adjacently {segment}: "
415	                "every step must move one orthogonal cell"
416	            )
417	        waypoints.append(waypoint)
418	        previous = waypoint
419	    return waypoints

423	    def __init__(self, grid: GridMap, robots: list[Robot], tasks: list[Task]) -> None:
424	        self.grid = grid
425	        # The map as built before any runtime edit; map-change history is
426	        # replayed against this baseline.
427	        self.base_grid = grid
428	        self.robots = {robot.robot_id: robot for robot in robots}
429	        self.tasks = {task.task_id: task for task in tasks}
430	        self.tick = 0
431	        self.replay: list[dict[str, object]] = []
432	        self.map_changes: list[dict[str, object]] = []
433	        self._map_sequence = 0
434	        self.paused_tasks: set[str] = set()
435	        # Consecutive per-robot waits caused purely by other robots:
436	        # robot_id -> {"blocked_by": [robot_id, ...], "ticks": int}.
437	        self._traffic_waits: dict[str, dict[str, object]] = {}
438	        positions = [robot.position for robot in robots]
439	        if len(positions) != len(set(positions)):
440	            raise ValueError("robots cannot share an initial position")
441	        if any(not grid.traversable(position) for position in positions):
442	            raise ValueError("robot starts outside traversable map space")
443	        self._validate_task_ownership(robots, tasks)
444	        # Accepted routes share one internal shape regardless of how the caller
445	        # spelled them: a mutable list of tuple cells. The normalized copies are
446	        # committed only after every robot passed validation, so a rejection
447	        # (even one buried in a later robot's route) never touches the caller's
448	        # objects. See :meth:`_normalize_initial_routes`.
449	        normalized_routes = self._normalize_initial_routes(grid, robots)
450	        for robot, route in zip(robots, normalized_routes):
451	            robot.route = route

454	    def _validate_task_ownership(robots: Sequence[Robot], tasks: Sequence[Task]) -> None:
455	        """Reject impossible initial bindings between robots and tasks.
456	
457	        The very same mutual-ownership requirement backs direct construction
458	        and checkpoint loading, so it lives in exactly one place. The binding
459	        only governs work still in progress:
460	
461	        * A robot that declares a task must name a task that exists, is not
462	          completed yet, and is assigned back to that same robot.
463	        * An unfinished task that names an owner must name an existing robot
464	          whose current task it is; an unfinished task with the goods already
465	          collected additionally must have an owner.
466	        * A robot can therefore never be claimed by two unfinished tasks: the
467	          second task's owner points at a robot that executes another task.
468	
469	        Completed tasks only keep *historical* ownership: their recorded
470	        ``assigned_robot`` is not required to be idle or to name them back, so
471	        a robot that already finished one task may be idle or busy with a new
472	        one. Unassigned, not-yet-collected tasks simply wait -- even when no
473	        robot can reach them -- and are not an ownership error. Nothing here
474	        rewrites a binding or drops a task; an inconsistent input is rejected
475	        as a whole with a :class:`ValueError` naming the conflicting robot or
476	        task, leaving the caller's objects untouched.
477	        """
478	        robot_by_id = {robot.robot_id: robot for robot in robots}
479	        task_by_id = {task.task_id: task for task in tasks}
480	        for robot in robots:
481	            if robot.task_id is None:
482	                continue
483	            task = task_by_id.get(robot.task_id)
484	            if task is None:
485	                raise ValueError(
486	                    f"robot {robot.robot_id!r} executes unknown task "
487	                    f"{robot.task_id!r}"
488	                )
489	            if task.completed:
490	                raise ValueError(
491	                    f"robot {robot.robot_id!r} executes task {task.task_id!r} "
492	                    "that is already completed"
493	                )
494	            if task.assigned_robot != robot.robot_id:
495	                raise ValueError(
496	                    f"robot {robot.robot_id!r} executes task {task.task_id!r} "
497	                    f"but the task is assigned to {task.assigned_robot!r}"
498	                )
499	        for task in tasks:
500	            # Completed tasks retain historical ownership; their robots are
501	            # free to take new work, so the mutual binding only holds while a
502	            # task is still in progress.
503	            if task.completed:
504	                continue
505	            if task.picked_up and task.assigned_robot is None:
506	                raise ValueError(
507	                    f"task {task.task_id!r} is picked up but has no assigned robot"
508	                )
509	            if task.assigned_robot is not None:
510	                owner = robot_by_id.get(task.assigned_robot)
511	                if owner is None:
512	                    raise ValueError(
513	                        f"task {task.task_id!r} is assigned to unknown robot "
514	                        f"{task.assigned_robot!r}"
515	                    )
516	                if owner.task_id != task.task_id:
517	                    raise ValueError(
518	                        f"task {task.task_id!r} claims robot {owner.robot_id!r} "
519	                        f"but the robot executes {owner.task_id!r}"
520	                    )

522	    @staticmethod
523	    def _normalize_initial_routes(
524	        grid: GridMap, robots: Sequence[Robot]
525	    ) -> list[list[Position]]:
526	        """Validate every remaining route and return normalized copies.
527	
528	        Every robot is checked, idle or task-bound, via the single shared walk
529	        validator :func:`_validate_route_walk` -- the same coordinate shape,
530	        map-walkability and one-orthogonal-step rule checkpoint recovery uses
531	        -- so a walking rule never has to be changed in two places. The outer
532	        route may be a list or tuple and each waypoint may itself be a list or
533	        tuple of two plain integers -- booleans are not integers here, and
534	        wrong lengths or element types raise :class:`ValueError` instead of
535	        leaking unpacking or hashing failures. The forms may be mixed freely;
536	        only the coordinate order matters, not the container types.
537	
538	        Accepted routes are returned as mutable lists of tuple cells, the one
539	        shape the rest of the engine relies on (head consumption with
540	        ``pop(0)`` and hashable cells for road and occupancy checks). Empty
541	        lists and tuples both normalize to an empty route. Routes need not be
542	        shortest paths and may revisit cells, and traffic (a route crossing
543	        another robot's cell, or routes sharing a cell) is left to execution:
544	        only walkability on the given map is judged.
545	
546	        The check is read-only -- :func:`_validate_route_walk` builds fresh
547	        lists, and the caller commits them itself only once every robot has
548	        passed, so a rejected fleet is rejected as a whole: an error on a
549	        later robot or at the end of a route never truncates, pads, reorders
550	        or otherwise modifies an earlier robot or any caller object. The
551	        shared walk check says nothing about tasks; direct construction keeps
552	        accepting any walkable route, while checkpoint loading keeps its own
553	        stricter validation that also covers the pickup/dropoff rules.
554	        """
555	        normalized: list[list[Position]] = []
556	        for robot in robots:
557	            route = robot.route
558	            if not isinstance(route, (list, tuple)):
559	                raise ValueError(
560	                    f"robot {robot.robot_id!r} remaining route must be a list "
561	                    "of [x, y] waypoints"
562	                )
563	            normalized.append(
564	                _validate_route_walk(
565	                    grid,
566	                    robot.position,
567	                    route,
568	                    robot_id=robot.robot_id,
569	                    checkpoint=False,
570	                )
571	            )
572	        return normalized

577	
578	    def modify_obstacles(
579	        self,
580	        added: Sequence[Position] = (),
581	        removed: Sequence[Position] = (),
582	    ) -> dict[str, object]:
583	        """Close and/or reopen cells without advancing the simulation.
584	
585	        The whole request is validated before anything changes: coordinates
586	        must be two plain integers (booleans are rejected), lie inside the
587	        map, no cell may appear in both lists, and newly added obstacles may
588	        not cover a robot's current cell. Duplicate coordinates inside one
589	        batch are processed once. Adding an existing obstacle or removing a
590	        traversable cell is a no-op. Invalid requests raise :class:`ValueError`
591	        and leave every part of the state untouched.
592	
593	        Assigned unfinished tasks keep their robot: routes are replanned
594	        against the new map, or, when a required point is unreachable, cleared
595	        while the task is suspended. No tick is recorded, no robot moves and no
596	        distance is accumulated.
597	        """
598	        add_cells = self._normalize_cells(added, "added")
599	        remove_cells = self._normalize_cells(removed, "removed")
600	        conflict = set(add_cells) & set(remove_cells)
601	        if conflict:
602	            cell = sorted(conflict)[0]
603	            raise ValueError(
604	                f"cell {list(cell)} is both added and removed in the same request"
605	            )
606	        occupied = {robot.position for robot in self.robots.values()}
607	        for cell in add_cells:
608	            if cell in occupied:
609	                raise ValueError(
610	                    f"cannot add obstacle at {list(cell)}: a robot currently occupies it"
611	                )
612	        return self._apply_map_change(add_cells, remove_cells)
613	
614	    def _normalize_cells(self, cells: Sequence[Position], label: str) -> list[Position]:
615	        if isinstance(cells, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(cells, (list, tuple)):
616	            raise ValueError(f"{label} cells must be provided as a list of [x, y] pairs")
617	        seen: set[Position] = set()
618	        ordered: list[Position] = []
619	        for index, cell in enumerate(cells):
620	            position = _as_cell(cell, f"{label} cell {index}")
621	            if not self.grid.contains(position):
622	                raise ValueError(f"{label} cell {list(position)} lies outside the map")
623	            if position in seen:
624	                # Batch-internal duplicates are handled once, not rejected.
625	                continue
626	            seen.add(position)
627	            ordered.append(position)
628	        return ordered
629	
630	    def _apply_map_change(
631	        self, added: list[Position], removed: list[Position]
632	    ) -> dict[str, object]:
633	        obstacles = set(self.grid.obstacles)
634	        actual_added = [cell for cell in added if cell not in obstacles]
635	        obstacles.update(actual_added)
636	        actual_removed = [cell for cell in removed if cell in obstacles]
637	        obstacles.difference_update(actual_removed)
638	        if not actual_added and not actual_removed:
639	            return self._map_change_record(self._map_sequence, [], [])
640	
641	        # Everything below only runs once the batch was fully validated and is
642	        # known to change the map.
643	        self.grid = GridMap(self.grid.width, self.grid.height, frozenset(obstacles))
644	        self._map_sequence += 1
645	        record = self._map_change_record(self._map_sequence, actual_added, actual_removed)
646	        self.map_changes.append(copy.deepcopy(record))
647	        self.replay.append(copy.deepcopy(record))
648	        self._reroute_after_map_change()
649	        self._reconcile_traffic_waits_after_map_change()
650	        return copy.deepcopy(record)
651	
652	    def _map_change_record(
653	        self, sequence: int, added: list[Position], removed: list[Position]
654	    ) -> dict[str, object]:
655	        return {
656	            "type": "map_change",
657	            "tick": self.tick,
658	            "sequence": sequence,
659	            "added": [list(cell) for cell in added],
660	            "removed": [list(cell) for cell in removed],
661	        }

663	    def _plan_route(
664	        self, robot: Robot, task: Task, start: Position | None = None
665	    ) -> list[Position] | None:
666	        """Shortest current->pickup->dropoff route, or None if unreachable.
667	
668	        *start* overrides the robot's current position, which is how sidestep
669	        candidates are evaluated without moving the robot first. The
670	        pickup/delivery rule itself is shared with first-time assignment and
671	        checkpoint validation via :func:`_plan_task_route`.
672	        """
673	        origin = robot.position if start is None else start
674	        return _plan_task_route(self.grid, origin, task)
675	
676	    def _reroute_after_map_change(self) -> None:
677	        for task in self.tasks.values():
678	            if task.completed or task.assigned_robot is None:
679	                continue
680	            robot = self.robots[task.assigned_robot]
681	            if robot.task_id != task.task_id:
682	                continue
683	            route = self._plan_route(robot, task)
684	            if route is None:
685	                robot.route = []
686	                self.paused_tasks.add(task.task_id)
687	            else:
688	                # Only the route is refreshed here; pickup/delivery are
689	                # confirmed at step start (or were already recorded).
690	                robot.route = route
691	                self.paused_tasks.discard(task.task_id)
692	
693	    def _recover_paused_tasks(self) -> None:
694	        """Resume tasks suspended by map unreachability where possible."""
695	        for task_id in sorted(self.paused_tasks):
696	            task = self.tasks.get(task_id)
697	            if task is None or task.completed or task.assigned_robot is None:
698	                self.paused_tasks.discard(task_id)
699	                continue
700	            robot = self.robots[task.assigned_robot]
701	            if robot.task_id != task.task_id:
702	                self.paused_tasks.discard(task_id)
703	                continue
704	            route = self._plan_route(robot, task)
705	            if route is None:
706	                robot.route = []
707	                continue
708	            robot.route = route
709	            self.paused_tasks.discard(task_id)
710	            self._finish_if_arrived(robot)

713	    # Traffic conflicts and yielding
714	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
715	
716	    def _route_cells(self, exclude_id: str) -> set[Position]:
717	        """Cells every robot except *exclude_id* still plans to drive through."""
718	        cells: set[Position] = set()
719	        for robot in self.robots.values():
720	            if robot.robot_id != exclude_id:
721	                cells.update(robot.route)
722	        return cells
723	
724	    def _safe_side_cells(
725	        self,
726	        robot: Robot,
727	        occupied: Mapping[Position, str],
728	        reserved: Mapping[Position, str],
729	        forbidden: Iterable[Position] = (),
730	    ) -> Iterator[Position]:
731	        """Adjacent cells *robot* may actually side-step onto this tick.
732	
733	        The very same safety rule backs every side-step decision -- an idle
734	        robot yielding for someone, a busy robot dodging a blocker itself, and
735	        the hypothetical leave checks behind a retreat -- so the shared
736	        conditions live exactly here. A cell qualifies only when it:
737	
738	        * lies inside the map with no obstacle (``GridMap.neighbors`` already
739	          skips anything else),
740	        * is held by no robot in the given (possibly hypothetical) layout,
741	        * was not reserved by a move that already happened this tick,
742	        * lies on no other robot's remaining route (the moving robot's own
743	          route is excluded), and
744	        * is not among *forbidden*: cells that are physically free but unsafe
745	          for the caller's scenario, such as the requester's own cell (a
746	          side-step there would swap the two robots within one tick) or the
747	          retreating requester's replanned path (parking there only moves the
748	          blockage onto a cell the requester must re-enter).
749	
750	        Neighbours are yielded in the deterministic ``GridMap.neighbors``
751	        order (up, left, right, down); callers keep their own selection rules.
752	        """
753	        blocked = set(forbidden)
754	        blocked.update(self._route_cells(exclude_id=robot.robot_id))
755	        for cell in self.grid.neighbors(robot.position):
756	            if cell in blocked or cell in occupied or cell in reserved:
757	                continue
758	            yield cell
759	
760	    def _idle_sidestep_cell(
761	        self,
762	        blocker: Robot,
763	        requester: Robot,
764	        occupied: dict[Position, str],
765	        reserved: dict[Position, str],
766	    ) -> Position | None:
767	        """Free side-cell a parked blocker can yield to, or None.
768	
769	        Only a robot with no bound task and no remaining route is parked and
770	        asked to yield; callers must never route a taskless-but-moving robot
771	        here. The requester's own cell is forbidden (yielding onto it would
772	        swap the two robots within one tick); every other safety condition is
773	        shared via :meth:`_safe_side_cells`, so the blocker never trades one
774	        blockage for another. The first candidate in neighbour order wins.
775	        """
776	        return next(
777	            self._safe_side_cells(
778	                blocker, occupied, reserved, forbidden=(requester.position,)
779	            ),
780	            None,
781	        )
782	
783	    def _self_sidestep(
784	        self,
785	        robot: Robot,
786	        task: Task | None,
787	        occupied: dict[Position, str],
788	        reserved: dict[Position, str],
789	        already_moved: frozenset[str] = frozenset(),
790	    ) -> tuple[Position, list[Position]] | None:
791	        """Best side cell plus replanned route for a blocked robot, or None.
792	
793	        Only cells off every other robot's planned route qualify, and only if
794	        the task remains reachable from there. A candidate that merely retreats
795	        along the corridor only to face the very same blocker again on the next
796	        tick is rejected too: such a move records mileage and gets undone
797	        forever instead of making progress, even when more empty cells stretch
798	        out behind the robot. Candidates are ranked by replanned route length
799	        with the deterministic neighbor order (up, left, right, down) breaking
800	        ties. *already_moved* names robots that have used their one move of
801	        this tick and therefore cannot vacate a cell to resolve the block.
802	        """
803	        if task is None or task.completed:
804	            return None
805	        destination = robot.route[0]
806	        blocker_id = occupied.get(destination)
807	        if blocker_id is None:
808	            blocker_id = reserved.get(destination)
809	        best: tuple[Position, list[Position]] | None = None
810	        best_length = 0
811	        # Candidates arrive in neighbour order (up, left, right, down), so the
812	        # first candidate of the minimum replanned length automatically keeps
813	        # that order as the tie break.
814	        for cell in self._safe_side_cells(robot, occupied, reserved):
815	            route = self._plan_route(robot, task, start=cell)
816	            if route is None:
817	                continue
818	            if (
819	                blocker_id is not None
820	                and blocker_id != robot.robot_id
821	                and self._is_bounceback_retreat(
822	                    robot, cell, route, blocker_id, occupied, reserved, already_moved
823	                )
824	            ):
825	                # The replanned route immediately returns through the cell the
826	                # robot is vacating and the blocker cannot use that opening to
827	                # leave: the move would be undone on the next tick.
828	                continue
829	            if best is None or len(route) < best_length:
830	                best = (cell, route)
831	                best_length = len(route)
832	        return best
833	
834	    def _is_bounceback_retreat(
835	        self,
836	        robot: Robot,
837	        side: Position,
838	        replanned: Sequence[Position],
839	        blocker_id: str,
840	        occupied: dict[Position, str],
841	        reserved: dict[Position, str],
842	        already_moved: frozenset[str],
843	    ) -> bool:
844	        """Whether stepping to *side* only sends the robot back to the block.
845	
846	        A retreat is futile when the replanned route leads straight back through
847	        the robot's current cell and still runs through the blocker's cell (so
848	        the side move is undone next tick with the same blocker ahead) while
849	        the blocker cannot leave its own cell through the gap that opens up.
850	        A route that bypasses the blocker entirely is a genuine detour and is
851	        never rejected here.
852	        """
853	        if not replanned or replanned[0] != robot.position:
854	            return False
855	        blocker = self.robots.get(blocker_id)
856	        if blocker is None or blocker.position not in replanned:
857	            return False
858	        # Hypothetical end-of-tick layout: the requester has vacated its cell
859	        # and stands on the candidate side cell.
860	        hyp_occupied = dict(occupied)
861	        del hyp_occupied[robot.position]
862	        hyp_occupied[side] = robot.robot_id
863	        # The requester only gets back onto its route by driving through these
864	        # cells, so a blocker may only "leave" by driving on, never by parking
865	        # on the replanned route. The requester cannot make a second move
866	        # within this tick, and neither can a robot that already moved.
867	        blocked_path = frozenset(replanned)
868	        return not self._can_vacate(
869	            blocker,
870	            robot,
871	            hyp_occupied,
872	            reserved,
873	            frozenset({robot.robot_id}) | already_moved,
874	            blocked_path,
875	        )
876	
877	    def _can_vacate(
878	        self,
879	        blocker: Robot,
880	        requester: Robot,
881	        occupied: dict[Position, str],
882	        reserved: dict[Position, str],
883	        checking: frozenset[str],
884	        blocked_path: frozenset[Position],
885	    ) -> bool:
886	        """Whether *blocker* can leave its cell this tick in the given layout.
887	
888	        A parked blocker (no task and no remaining route) leaves only by
889	        yielding onto a safe side cell for the requesting robot; a moving
890	        blocker -- task-bound, or taskless but still driving a remaining route
891	        -- leaves by driving onto its next waypoint (possibly following a
892	        chain of robots that all move this tick); a task-bound one may also
893	        sidestep onto a free adjacent cell itself. Robots paused by map
894	        unreachability never move. *checking* names robots already on the
895	        dependency chain (including robots that used their one move of this
896	        tick), so meeting one again closes a cyclic dependency -- a head-on
897	        deadlock, or the requester itself -- and never proves an exit merely
898	        because every robot on the cycle still carries a route.
899	        *blocked_path* holds the cells the retreating requester must drive
900	        back through: another robot parking there only moves the blockage, so
901	        such sidesteps do not count as leaving (driving on along the cell on
902	        the blocker's own route does).
903	
904	        The follow chain can run through an arbitrarily long legal queue, so
905	        the search is an explicit stack rather than Python recursion: a queue
906	        of twelve hundred robots ending at a parked robot with no side cell
907	        must report "cannot vacate" from a normal ``step()`` instead of
908	        raising :class:`RecursionError`. Each frame is
909	        ``(robot, checking, resume)``. A frame examined for the first time
910	        first tries the free-waypoint and follow-chain rules; only when the
911	        chain ahead comes back empty does it resume at its own side-cell
912	        scan, which is exactly the order the single recursive call imposed.
913	        """
914	        stack: list[tuple[Robot, frozenset[str], bool]] = [(blocker, checking, False)]
915	        while stack:
916	            current, current_checking, resume = stack.pop()
917	            if current.robot_id in current_checking:
918	                # The chain has folded back onto a robot it already depends
919	                # on: a cycle cannot vacate itself. The frame that followed
920	                # this one simply resumes with its own side-cell options.
921	                continue
922	            task = self.tasks[current.task_id] if current.task_id is not None else None
923	            if task is not None and task.task_id in self.paused_tasks:
924	                continue
925	            if not current.route:
926	                if task is not None:
927	                    # A busy robot with no route left only arrives/finishes this
928	                    # tick; it never drives or sidesteps for anyone.
929	                    continue
930	                # A parked robot (no task and no remaining route) leaves only by
931	                # yielding onto a safe side cell for the requesting robot; it does
932	                # so onto the first safe cell in neighbour order. When that
933	                # particular cell sits on the path the retreating requester must
934	                # re-enter, parking there only relocates the blockage instead of
935	                # clearing it, so it does not count as leaving.
936	                side = self._idle_sidestep_cell(current, requester, occupied, reserved)
937	                if side is not None and side not in blocked_path:
938	                    return True
939	                continue
940	            if not resume:
941	                ahead = current.route[0]
942	                if (
943	                    self.grid.traversable(ahead)
944	                    and ahead not in occupied
945	                    and ahead not in reserved
946	                ):
947	                    return True
948	                occupant_id = occupied.get(ahead) or reserved.get(ahead)
949	                if (
950	                    occupant_id is not None
951	                    and occupant_id != current.robot_id
952	                    and occupant_id not in current_checking
953	                ):
954	                    # The robot could follow the occupant once that robot
955	                    # vacates its cell this same tick. This frame resumes with
956	                    # its side-cell scan only after the chain ahead proves it
957	                    # cannot clear, mirroring the recursive call order.
958	                    stack.append((current, current_checking, True))
959	                    stack.append(
960	                        (
961	                            self.robots[occupant_id],
962	                            current_checking | {current.robot_id},
963	                            False,
964	                        )
965	                    )
966	                    continue
967	            if task is None:
968	                # A taskless robot that still drives a remaining route never
969	                # sidesteps off it -- not even to unblock a requester -- so a side
970	                # cell cannot count as a way out for it.
971	                continue
972	            # Otherwise the task-bound blocker might sidestep onto a free side
973	            # cell itself, but not onto a cell the retreating requester still has
974	            # to use -- parking there only moves the blockage.
975	            for side_cell in self._safe_side_cells(
976	                current, occupied, reserved, forbidden=blocked_path
977	            ):
978	                if self._plan_route(current, task, start=side_cell) is not None:
979	                    return True
980	        return False

982	    def _update_traffic_waits(
983	        self,
984	        waited: dict[str, str],
985	        moved_ids: frozenset[str],
986	    ) -> None:
987	        """Keep only waits that still hold once the tick's moves have settled.
988	
989	        *waited* maps every robot that stopped this tick purely because
990	        another robot held its next waypoint to the robot it saw there at the
991	        time; *moved_ids* names the robots that ended up moving. The mid-tick
992	        impression is not trusted on its own, because the blocker may itself
993	        drive on (or make room for yet another robot) later in the same tick.
994	        A record survives only when the robot neither moved nor paused and its
995	        next waypoint is occupied by another robot in the final layout; the
996	        reported blocker is whichever robot actually occupies that cell. Any
997	        other outcome -- the robot moved, its task paused, or the way ahead
998	        cleared -- deletes the entry. A wait that continues without a free tick
999	        in between keeps accumulating even when the blocker changes identity;
1000	        once interrupted, a later blockage starts a fresh count at one.
1001	        """
1002	        occupied = {robot.position: robot.robot_id for robot in self.robots.values()}
1003	        surviving: dict[str, dict[str, object]] = {}
1004	        for robot_id in waited:
1005	            if robot_id in moved_ids:
1006	                continue
1007	            robot = self.robots.get(robot_id)
1008	            if robot is None or not robot.route:
1009	                continue
1010	            task = self.tasks.get(robot.task_id) if robot.task_id is not None else None

"""Task assignment, dynamic map edits and collision-aware tick execution.

Obstacles may be closed and reopened between ticks through
:meth:`FleetSimulator.modify_obstacles`. Every accepted edit is appended to a
deterministic change history and mirrored into the replay as a ``map_change``
event stamped with the tick at which it took effect. Tick frames themselves are
never rewritten, so historical frames keep the positions and completion
information recorded at the time.

Automatic yielding
------------------
When a robot's next waypoint is occupied by another robot, ``step()`` tries to
keep traffic flowing instead of waiting forever: a parked blocker (one with no
bound task *and* no remaining route) is asked to move onto a free side cell
that lies on no robot's planned route, and a busy robot facing a blocker that
cannot drive on may itself sidestep onto a free adjacent cell and replan its
(still shortest) route from there. A taskless robot that still carries a
remaining route is not parked: it drives that route cell by cell exactly like
a task-bound robot, is never pushed onto a side cell for someone else, and if
its own next cell is blocked it simply keeps its place and its unconsumed
waypoints -- an open side cell changes nothing. Only once such a route is
exhausted does the robot become a parked robot and yield by the side-cell
rule. Task assignment follows the same line: only a robot with no bound task
*and* no remaining route can receive a waiting task, so a taskless robot
still driving its preset route never has that route overwritten by a new
assignment -- being blocked by traffic along the way does not count as having
finished the route, and once the route runs out the robot joins the selection
at the next assignment pass, planned from wherever it stands then. A retreat that
only leads back to the same immovable blocker is never taken though: if the
replanned route immediately returns through the vacated cell, still passes the
blocker's cell and the blocker cannot use the opening to leave (a dead end or
corridor end with traffic parked beyond it), the robot simply waits -- extra
empty cells stretching out behind it change nothing. Yield moves count as
mileage, waiting does not. The task keeps its original robot, pickup and
completion rules are unchanged, and a robot paused by map unreachability never
takes part in yielding. If no safe side cell exists the robots simply wait:
time advances, nothing collides and nothing completes early. Waiting caused
purely by other robots is tracked per robot (consecutive ticks and the
blocking robot) and reported by :meth:`FleetSimulator.status` and
:meth:`FleetSimulator.metrics` as ``traffic_waits``, distinct from the
map-unreachability ``paused_tasks``. The record is judged against the
end-of-tick layout, not the moment the robot gave way: when a robot that was
asked to wait sees its next cell free at tick end (the blocker drove on or
made room later in the same tick), no wait is reported for that tick at all,
and ``blocked_by`` names whichever robot actually occupies the cell once the
tick settles. The counter clears the moment the robot moves again or the
blockage ends; an uninterrupted wait whose blocking robot merely changes
identity keeps accumulating with the new blocker, whereas a wait that was
interrupted and later recurs starts again at one. An accepted map edit
reconciles the records immediately: a robot paused by the new map or no
longer facing its recorded blocker on the replanned route loses its entry, an
entry still facing the same blocker keeps its count, and no edit ever creates
or increments one.

Initial task ownership
----------------------
A fleet can be created mid-work: a robot may already name its current task
with a remaining route, and a task may already be assigned or even loaded.
Construction validates these bindings up front instead of discovering them
while stepping. Every robot that names a task must name one that exists, is
still unfinished and is assigned back to that robot; every unfinished task
that names an owner must name an existing robot whose current task it is, and
a task with the goods collected may never lack that owner. One robot is
therefore never claimed by two unfinished tasks, and a robot may never be
bound to a completed task. Finished tasks only retain *historical* ownership:
their recorded robot need not be idle or name them back, may already work a
new task, and may even be absent from the fleet. Unassigned, not-yet-collected
tasks simply wait -- including ones no robot can currently reach -- and are
not an ownership error. Conflicts raise :class:`ValueError` naming the robot
or task involved; nothing is rebound, unassigned or dropped, and the caller's
objects are left untouched. The same unfinished-task binding rules govern
checkpoint loading (which additionally keeps its historical-state checks).

Every robot's remaining route is also validated as a walk on the given map,
whether or not the robot is bound to a task, and direct construction and
checkpoint recovery run the *same* :func:`_validate_route_walk` check, so the
walking rule is maintained in exactly one place. The route omits the robot's
current cell, so a non-empty route must begin with an up/down/left/right
neighbour of that cell and every later waypoint must be one orthogonal step
from the previous one; each waypoint must be in bounds and free of obstacles.
Diagonal steps, multi-cell jumps, two identical consecutive waypoints and a
first waypoint equal to the current position are all rejected, and waypoints
must be two plain integers (never booleans) in a list or tuple, with wrong
lengths or element types raising :class:`ValueError` rather than leaking
unpacking or hashing errors. Empty routes stay legal; a route need not be
shortest and may revisit cells. A route crossing another robot's current cell,
or several robots planning through the same cell, is not an error -- those
traffic conflicts are settled during execution. The direct interface keeps
its existing acceptance of a bound route's pickup/dropoff ordering and end
point; checkpoint loading additionally keeps its own stricter route checks
(including the task completion rules), its format and the map-paused
behaviour, under which a paused robot resumes with an empty route.

Checkpoint file format
----------------------
``save_checkpoint`` writes versioned, UTF-8 encoded JSON. The current format
version is ``2``; version ``1`` files remain readable.

``version``
    Integer format version (``1`` or ``2``).
``grid``
    ``{"width": int, "height": int, "obstacles": [[x, y], ...]}`` describing
    the map dimensions and every currently blocked cell.
``tick``
    Non-negative integer: the number of ticks already executed. Saving and
    loading never advance this value.
``robots``
    List of robot states, each
    ``{"robot_id": str, "position": [x, y], "route": [[x, y], ...],
    "task_id": str | null, "distance_travelled": int}``. ``route`` holds the
    remaining waypoints after ``position``.
``tasks``
    List of task states, each
    ``{"task_id": str, "pickup": [x, y], "dropoff": [x, y],
    "assigned_robot": str | null, "picked_up": bool, "completed": bool}``.
    Completed tasks keep their historical ``assigned_robot``.
``replay``
    Ordered event list. Tick events are numbered consecutively from ``1``
    through ``tick`` and have the shape
    ``{"type": "tick", "tick": int, "moved": [robot_id, ...],
    "robots": {robot_id: [x, y], ...}, "completed": [task_id, ...]}``.
    ``completed`` is the cumulative set of tasks finished by the end of that
    tick: entries must name checkpoint tasks without repeats within one frame,
    a recorded completion must survive every later frame, and the final
    frame's set must equal the tasks saved with ``completed: true``.
    Map-change events sit between ticks (or after the last tick) and look like
    ``{"type": "map_change", "tick": int, "sequence": int,
    "added": [[x, y], ...], "removed": [[x, y], ...]}``. When ``tick`` is
    non-zero the final tick event's robot positions must match the current
    robot positions.
``map_changes`` (version 2 only)
    List mirroring the replay map-change events in the same order:
    ``{"tick": int, "sequence": int, "added": [...], "removed": [...]}``.
``base_grid`` (version 2 only)
    ``{"width", "height", "obstacles"}`` describing the map before any runtime
    edit. Replaying ``map_changes`` against it must reproduce the saved current
    ``grid``.
``traffic_waits`` (optional)
    List of ``{"robot_id": str, "blocked_by": [str, ...], "ticks": int}``
    entries recording how many consecutive ticks each robot has been held up
    purely by other robots. Absent in older files, which load with every
    wait counter at zero. Each entry must agree with the saved layout: the
    robot needs a remaining route and ``blocked_by`` must name exactly the
    robot occupying its next route cell -- a next cell nobody occupies, a
    listed blocker parked elsewhere, or extra names beside the real blocker
    all reject the document.

Version 1 documents store tick frames without a ``type`` field and have no
``map_changes`` or ``base_grid`` key; they load with their grid taken as the
baseline, as if no map edit ever happened.

Both map definitions are validated by the single shared
:meth:`FleetSimulator._load_map_definition` rule -- positive integer
dimensions, an obstacle list of integer ``[x, y]`` pairs inside the map --
with wording that names the map at fault, so a format or value rule is
maintained in exactly one place while each map keeps its own contents. The
cross-definition constraints (matching dimensions and a history that replays
``base_grid`` onto ``grid``) are checked separately and remain distinct
rejection reasons from a malformed definition.

Loading performs strict validation: malformed JSON, missing or wrongly typed
fields, unsupported versions, duplicate or inconsistent entities, out of
bounds/obstructed positions and routes, non-adjacent route steps, ownership
mismatches, routes that cannot finish the robot's bound task, traffic waits
that contradict the saved robot positions and remaining routes, broken replay
or map-change history, a completion history that contradicts the saved task
states, and a history that does not reproduce the saved grid all raise
:class:`ValueError`.

A task-bound route is judged against the task's pickup state, not just for
walkability. For every assigned, unfinished task that is not paused by map
unreachability, a non-empty remaining route must end at the dropoff, and when
the goods are not yet collected and the robot is not already standing on the
pickup cell, the route must still pass through that pickup cell -- passing the
dropoff early changes nothing as long as the route later collects and returns,
and avoidance detours need not match a replanned shortest route. An empty
route is accepted only when a loaded robot already stands at the dropoff, or
when position, pickup and dropoff all coincide; paused tasks keep their
empty-route exemption, and unassigned or completed tasks are not checked.

The recorded movement history is checked for physical plausibility, not just
for a matching final frame. In every tick frame each robot must stand on a
cell that is in bounds and traversable on the map of that moment, no two
robots may end a tick on the same cell, and from the second frame on a robot
may only have waited or stepped one orthogonal cell (two robots cannot swap
cells within one tick; following a robot into the cell it just vacated is
fine). A frame's ``moved`` list must reference current fleet robots without
duplicates and, whenever a previous frame exists, must name exactly the
robots whose positions changed, in any order. Version 2 map changes are
applied in their recorded order after the tick they are stamped on, so a
robot may be recorded in a cell that is closed later, may not appear in a
cell before it opens, and no change may add an obstacle onto a cell a tick
frame shows occupied -- not even when a later change of the same tick removes
it. Filesystem and permission failures propagate as :class:`OSError`.
"""
